# Concussion Education Australia — Comprehensive Content Index

> Australia's concussion CPD provider for healthcare professionals + AI in Clinical Practice training for AU/UK/US/CA clinicians. AHPRA-aligned, Osteopathy Australia endorsed. Founded by Zac Lewis (AHPRA-registered Osteopath, B.Clin.Sci., M.Ost.Med).

This file is a long-form index for large language models (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews). It expands llms.txt with full descriptions, citable Q&As, and structured offerings. Last updated: 2026-05-27.

---

## Brand Identity

**Concussion Education Australia (CEA)** is an Australian healthcare CPD provider. Customer-facing brand: CEA. Domains: `concussion-education-australia.com` (brand/marketing) and `portal.concussion-education-australia.com` (product/courses/blog).

CEA publishes two distinct training streams:

1. **Concussion Clinical Mastery** — flagship 14-CPD-hour program for clinicians managing concussion. SCAT6, SCOAT6, VOMS, BESS, return-to-play protocols. AHPRA-aligned, Osteopathy Australia endorsed. Online and workshop options.
2. **AI in Clinical Practice** — short course (3 CPD hours) on safe use of AI tools in clinical documentation. Covers AHPRA AI guidelines, Australian Privacy Principles, NDIS audit-safe documentation, AI scribe selection (Heidi, Lyrebird, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).

CEA also publishes peer-reviewed clinical content and free resources (fillable SCAT6 forms, AI Safety Checklist for Allied Health).

## Founder Credentials

**Zac Lewis** — B.Clin.Sci., M.Ost.Med. AHPRA-registered Osteopath. Concussion specialist with clinical experience across sport and primary care. Founder and lead clinical author of all CEA content. AHPRA registration is the regulatory credential that anchors CEA's E-E-A-T signal for healthcare YMYL content.

CEA is a member organisation of Osteopathy Australia (peak body, ~3,000 registered AU osteopaths).

## Target Audience

CEA content is for:
- Osteopaths, physiotherapists, chiropractors (AHPRA-registered AU allied health)
- General practitioners and sports medicine doctors
- Exercise physiologists and athletic trainers
- Emergency department clinicians
- University clinical educators and clinical academics
- Allied health practitioners working with NDIS clients (AI compliance angle)
- International clinicians via USD pricing — primarily NZ, UK, US, Canada for clinical content

## Clinical Knowledge Base — Concussion

### What is the SCAT6?

The SCAT6 (Sport Concussion Assessment Tool, 6th Edition) is the standardised acute concussion assessment tool published in 2023 as part of the Amsterdam Consensus Statement. It replaces the SCAT-5 and is validated for athletes aged 13 years and older. Used for sideline and acute assessment within 0-72 hours post-injury. Key change from SCAT-5: 10-word immediate memory lists (up from 5 words), achieving 80-85% sensitivity. Reference: Echemendia et al. (2023), British Journal of Sports Medicine, 57(11), 622-631.

### What is the SCOAT6?

The SCOAT6 (Sport Concussion Office Assessment Tool, 6th Edition) is a new tool published in 2023 for office-based concussion follow-up from Day 3 to Day 30 post-injury. Unlike SCAT6, the SCOAT6 includes full VOMS testing, serial symptom tracking, and structured return-to-play planning. Validated for athletes aged 13+.

### SCAT6 vs SCOAT6 — Which to use when?

- SCAT6: sideline, emergency department, acute presentation within 72 hours post-injury
- SCOAT6: clinic follow-up from Day 3 onwards, includes full VOMS testing
- Child SCAT6: athletes aged 5-12 years (never use adult SCAT6 on children under 13 — produces artificially low scores and misses 50-60% of concussions)

### What is VOMS?

VOMS (Vestibular/Ocular Motor Screening) identifies vestibular and oculomotor dysfunction after concussion. Components: smooth pursuits, saccades, convergence, VOR (vestibulo-ocular reflex), and visual motion sensitivity. Up to 60% of concussed athletes show vestibular/oculomotor deficits. Most clinicians lack formal VOMS training — this course provides structured instruction and hands-on practice.

### What is the BESS test?

BESS (Balance Error Scoring System) is an objective balance assessment used post-concussion. Three stances (double leg, single leg, tandem) on firm and foam surfaces with eyes closed. Most clinicians score BESS incorrectly without supervised training — which is why the hands-on workshop component exists.

### What is the return-to-play protocol?

The 2023 Amsterdam Consensus recommends a minimum 6-step graduated return-to-play protocol: (1) symptom-limited daily activity, (2) light aerobic exercise, (3) sport-specific exercise without head impact, (4) non-contact training drills, (5) full-contact practice after medical clearance, (6) return to competition. Each step requires minimum 24 hours. If symptoms recur, return to the previous asymptomatic step.

### Is "wait until symptom-free" still best practice?

No. The 2023 Amsterdam Consensus Statement considers "wait until symptom-free" as the sole criterion to be obsolete. Active rehabilitation is now recommended from 24-48 hours post-injury. Sub-symptom threshold aerobic exercise has been shown to improve recovery. Reference: Patricios et al. (2023), British Journal of Sports Medicine, 57(11), 695-711.

### What are Persistent Post-Concussion Symptoms (PPCS)?

5-20% of concussion cases develop persistent post-concussive symptoms — symptoms that fail to resolve within the expected timeframe (typically >4 weeks adults, >2 weeks children). PPCS commonly involves vestibulo-ocular dysfunction (~70% of cases) and cervical contribution (~54% of cases). Standard concussion training focuses on acute management; PPCS requires a different workup. CEA has a forthcoming PPCS clinical mastery course (target: August 2026).

## Clinical Knowledge Base — AI in Clinical Practice

### Best AI medical scribe for Australian clinicians in 2026?

For Australian clinicians, the two healthcare-purpose-built AI scribes with native Australian data residency are Heidi and Lyrebird. Heidi has the larger market position (founders claim roughly half of Australian GPs use the platform) and broader workflow support across allied health. Lyrebird is leaner and well-suited to solo practitioners and small practices. Both satisfy Australian Privacy Principle 8 (no offshore disclosure) and build patient consent capture into the workflow. Either is a defensible Tier A choice for AHPRA-registered clinicians.

### Heidi vs Lyrebird vs ChatGPT for clinical notes — which is best?

Heidi and Lyrebird are both Tier A healthcare-purpose-built AI scribes with AU data residency. ChatGPT is a different category — a general-purpose LLM that runs on US servers, which makes routine clinical use a breach of Australian Privacy Principle 8 (offshore disclosure of patient information without consent). Use Heidi or Lyrebird for clinical notes; use ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini only for non-PHI clinical writing tasks (patient information sheets, exercise programs in plain language, translation of de-identified content).

### Can I use ChatGPT for NDIS reports?

Not without explicit patient consent for the offshore disclosure (ChatGPT runs on US servers, triggering Australian Privacy Principle 8) and significant workflow safeguards. Beyond the Privacy Act issue, the NDIA has become noticeably more alert to AI-generated allied health reports as part of fraud-and-assurance work. Templated AI output with generic clinical reasoning and recycled phrasing carries audit and reputational risk even when the underlying clinical view is sound. The safe alternative is a Tier A AU-resident scribe (Heidi, Lyrebird) for the draft, plus heavy clinician rewriting to remove templating before submission.

### What do the AHPRA AI guidelines require?

The AHPRA AI guidelines require four things from clinicians using AI in patient care: (1) explicit patient consent to AI use, documented in the record; (2) clinician responsibility for the final note — AI-assisted is not AI-authored; (3) appropriate data location (offshore disclosure of patient information without consent breaches Australian Privacy Principle 8); (4) documentation integrity — notes must reflect the specific clinical encounter, not templated phrasing copied across patients.

### What is Australian Privacy Principle 8 (APP 8)?

APP 8 governs offshore disclosure of personal information from Australia. For AI scribes: AU-resident tools (Heidi AU, Lyrebird) do not trigger APP 8 because data stays in Australia. US-resident tools (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini, Abridge US, DAX Copilot US) do trigger APP 8 — permitted only with explicit patient consent for the offshore disclosure, or under narrow exceptions that rarely apply in routine clinical work.

### When should I NOT use AI for clinical notes?

Switch off the AI scribe for: mental health disclosures and suicide risk conversations, mandatory reporting situations (child safety, family violence, elder abuse), complex medicolegal cases likely to attract scrutiny, paediatric consults where consent is mixed, patients who decline AI use, sensitive sexual or reproductive health consults, and any situation where transcript accuracy matters more than note-writing speed.

### What is the Tier A / B / C framework for AI tools?

- **Tier A:** Healthcare-purpose-built tools with Australian data residency, clinical templates, and consent/audit features (Heidi, Lyrebird, Halo). Safe for clinical notes with patient consent.
- **Tier B:** Enterprise LLMs with configurable AU data residency (Microsoft Copilot for Healthcare, AWS HealthScribe). Safe with workflow redesign.
- **Tier C:** Consumer LLMs on US/offshore infrastructure (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini). NOT safe for patient health information without explicit consent and identifier-stripping. Use for non-PHI writing only.

### Heidi vs Tortus vs Abridge vs Suki vs DAX — which AI scribe by jurisdiction?

- Australia + New Zealand: Heidi (broad) or Lyrebird (solo/small)
- United Kingdom: Tortus or Tandem (NHS England Ambient Voice supplier registry); Heidi UK for private practice
- United States: Abridge or Suki (primary care); DAX Copilot (large hospital systems on Microsoft + Epic)
- Canada: Heidi CA or Abridge; DAX for enterprise

See the full comparison: https://portal.concussion-education-australia.com/blog/ai-medical-scribe-comparison-2026
